RewardsCompetitionsNewslettersWeather ForecastEuropeRussian attacks kill seven in Ukraine after Trump strikes diesel deal with PutinZelenskiy says deal ‘plays into Russia’s hands  – allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer’Rescue workers carry a body from the rubble of a residential building destroyed by a Russian airstrike in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on Saturday. Photograph: Kateryna Klochko/AP Sat Oct 10 2026 - 09:21 • 2 MIN READRussian strikes killed at least seven people in Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region, officials said on Saturday, a day after US president Donald Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel that Kyiv warned would help bankroll Moscow’s war.

Three children were among the seven people killed when Russian aerial bombs hit residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the regional military administration, said on Saturday.

At least 10 people were wounded in the attack.

Russia and Ukraine are locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line, more than four-and-a-half years since Moscow’s full-scale invasion.

Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian bombardments that have killed more than 55 people over the past four days.

The latest attacks came a day after  Trump said he had struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a reversal of years of US pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices in advance of the US midterm elections.

Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian president Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he had been expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia.

Instead, Trump announced that Russia would  immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and one million tons “immediately thereafter”.

Russia will deliver an additional three million tons “within a short period of time” after that, he wrote.

Trump’s shock announcement was in stark contrast to a sweeping Russia sanctions law he signed last month that aimed to  clamp down on the oil and gas revenues that fuel Russia’s war against Ukraine.

In a lengthy post online reacting to the deal, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Russia would repay it “with further terror and perfidy”. He cast it as an investment in the war, allowing it to be prolonged.

“It plays into Russia’s hands – allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.

According to a statement released by the Ukrainian Embassy in Washington,  Zelenskiy called it “a weak decision, unfortunately, a weak decision by strong partners”.

Trump announced the deal as his envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner were meeting Ukrainian officials in Miami to discuss a proposal to end the war.

“I believe our team is simply being used as a smokescreen. And that is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,”  Zelenskiy said. – AP
